title: Agent wait heuristics: replace sleep/poll loops with event-driven BRC message stream consumption
summary: Architecture analysis for Option C (full scope per HITL resolution): prompt audit, new typed blocking primitive `egg-orch message wait`, configurable --wait cap, true blocking on the in-memory message store, HEARTBEAT message type with structured state wired into HealthMonitor, full QUESTION removal (including reviewer preamble advertisement and BRC_HISTORY_TYPES), consensus_wrapper replacement with a new MessageType.CONSENSUS_REACHED broadcast for the final flavour, WSGI worker-model track, and single-idiom documentation. Work is decomposed into 7 independent tracks that can land in separate commits within a single PR.

reviewer_plan_revision_1_nacks.summary: TD-5 referenced a non-existent MessageType.CONSENSUS_CONFIRMED_FINAL. Reviewer verified at signals.py:1430-1475 that the distinction between pending and final is only in metadata ({'pending_acks': True} vs {'consensus_reached': bool}); both use the same MessageType.CONSENSUS_CONFIRMED value.
reviewer_plan_revision_1_nacks.resolution: Picked option (a) from reviewer's suggestions: introduce a NEW MessageType.CONSENSUS_REACHED that is emitted from signals.py:1469 IN ADDITION TO the existing CONSENSUS_CONFIRMED (final flavour). Additive, test-safe, zero-churn on existing consumers (they keep reading CONSENSUS_CONFIRMED with metadata). Track 6 message wait filters on the new type. TD-5, TD-7, and Track 6 all updated. Documented in new TD-8.

Reviewer UX implication documented: post-removal reviewers express unresolved ambiguity via NACK or by declining to ACK; no bus-free clarification channel exists by design (per HITL decision-5).

reviewer_plan_revision_1_nacks.summary: HEARTBEAT design in F5/TD-3 omits that HealthMonitor.last_heartbeat (health_monitor.py:229/249-262) is only updated by PROGRESS events with type='heartbeat' (line 130 subscription to EventType.PROGRESS_EMITTED). HealthMonitor already subscribes to EventType.MESSAGE_SENT (line 133) but _on_message_sent (line 330-360) only tracks message rate for throttling — it does NOT reset last_heartbeat. problem_statement.description: During pipeline issue-1762-membump (2026-04-22) multiple agents used sleep/poll anti-patterns that blackholed them for 5-10 minutes while actionable messages (NACKs, overseer nudges, peer proposals) sat unread in their inboxes. Root cause is a combination of (a) the BRC preamble's 'Keep polling' phrasing in pipelines.py:5959 and :6020 which nudges LLMs toward outer `for i in 1..N; do egg-orch message poll --wait 60; done` loops, (b) the 60-second hard cap on `--wait` in routes/messages.py:165 which forces *some* outer loop no matter what, (c) the absence of a typed 'wait for specific event' primitive so agents default to generic poll loops, (d) silent non-blocking fallback in the in-memory message store (routes/messages.py:181-184) that defeats `--wait > 0` in local/CI deploys, and (e) the absence of a heartbeat message type so overseer liveness inference relies on message timing rather than explicit state.
goals: Agents react to bus events in seconds, not minutes — bounded by reasoning latency, not sleep heuristics
BRC consensus turn-around is dominated by actual producer work, not agent-side wait loops
Overseer liveness inference reads explicit agent state (HEARTBEAT) rather than inferring from message timing
Local development and CI (in-memory store backend) exercise the same blocking semantics as production (Redis)
consensus_wrapper's own stay-alive loop is event-driven so it has the same cache-cost / latency profile as the agents it wraps
One canonical recommended idiom per wait scenario — no variance across agents
non_goals: Introduce a REQUEST/REPLY peer-addressed messaging subsystem to replace QUESTION (explicitly deferred per decision-5 HITL resolution)
Change SSE streaming or the /events endpoint shape
Refactor the BRC protocol state machine itself — only the wait primitives around it
Backward-incompatible changes to the message store schema or existing CLI flags

findings.title: 'Keep polling' preamble language causes LLM-driven outer loops
findings.description: The producer and reviewer lifecycle steps both end with 'STAY ALIVE: Keep polling egg-orch message poll --wait 30 until the orchestrator stops you.' This reads as a recurring action the agent must orchestrate. Combined with LLM training data rich in `for i in ...; do ...; done` and `while true; do ...; sleep N; done` idioms, it produces the exact anti-patterns observed in issue-1762-membump.
findings.remediation: Replace preamble with a single canonical idiom: `while true; do egg-orch message wait --for CONSENSUS_REACHED || break; done`. Add explicit Don'ts listing for-loop wrapping and `sleep N`. Covered in Track 1.

findings.title: 60s hard cap on --wait forces outer loops even for correct agents
findings.description: routes/messages.py:165 caps `wait` at 60s via `min(max(int(...), 0), 60)`. Even an agent that correctly uses `--wait 60` without a loop still has its connection close every 60s, and it will need *some* outer construct to keep re-entering the call. The line between 'single while-true loop' (acceptable) and 'for i in 1..N' (anti-pattern) is fuzzy for the LLM.
findings.remediation: Make the cap configurable via `EGG_MESSAGE_POLL_MAX_WAIT` (default 60s); document that raising it requires raising the HTTP proxy idle timeout in lockstep. Covered in Track 2. Raising the default is deferred — operators opt in.

findings.title: No typed 'wait for specific event' primitive
findings.description: Agents currently have `egg-orch message poll --wait N` (generic bulk fetch with timeout) and nothing else. When an agent wants to wait for a specific event (e.g. a final CONSENSUS_REACHED broadcast from all peers) it must wrap `message poll` in a loop and manually filter. The manual filtering encourages bespoke logic per agent.
findings.remediation: Introduce `egg-orch message wait --for TYPE [--from ROLE] [--timeout N] [--since ID]` (per decision-2). Server-side route loops over XREAD BLOCK with type/role filtering until a match is seen or timeout. Client gets a single response. Covered in Track 3.

findings.title: In-memory store silently falls back to non-blocking — breaks local dev and CI
findings.description: routes/messages.py:181-184 catches TypeError when `wait` kwarg is rejected by the in-memory store and retries without it. Q2 HITL resolution confirms local deploys run without Redis, so this is load-bearing for development, not just tests. Any new blocking primitive that uses this code path will silently false-green.
findings.remediation: Add a condition variable to `InMemoryMessageStore` and implement `get_messages(..., wait=N)` with true blocking semantics. Remove the `except TypeError` fallback in routes/messages.py — all stores must now support `wait`. MessageStore.clear() must notify_all to unblock pending waiters at phase transitions. Covered in Track 4.

findings.title: No HEARTBEAT message type — overseer infers liveness from message timing
findings.description: message_store.py:19-37 defines 13 message types, none of which is a structured state heartbeat. Overseer Tier 1 liveness checks infer from last-message timestamps, which conflates 'alive but correctly waiting' with 'stalled'. Agents sleeping through a NACK window look the same as crashed agents from this vantage point. Additionally, HealthMonitor._on_message_sent at line 330-360 subscribes to EventType.MESSAGE_SENT but does NOT reset last_heartbeat — so agents that emit HEARTBEAT instead of PROGRESS-heartbeat would still trip the heartbeat_timeout at line 400-460.
findings.remediation: Add `HEARTBEAT = 'HEARTBEAT'` with a structured metadata field `state` in {WORKING, WAITING_ON_ROLE, PROPOSED, CONFIRMED, IDLE}. Emit on state transitions (not periodically). Wire HealthMonitor._on_message_sent to reset last_heartbeat when message_type=='HEARTBEAT'. Hard rate limit at send_message validation (not just overseer log). Covered in Track 5.

findings.title: consensus_wrapper's own stay-alive loop mirrors the agent anti-pattern
findings.description: consensus_wrapper.py:322-351 runs a shell while-loop with 30s sleep between polls (10 cycles × 30s = 300s). Same cache-cost and responsiveness profile as the agent-side loops. SIGTERM handling is shell-level trap-based.
findings.remediation: Replace the shell loop with a single invocation of `egg-orch message wait --for CONSENSUS_REACHED --timeout $EGG_MESSAGE_POLL_MAX_WAIT`. Requires the new MessageType.CONSENSUS_REACHED emitted at signals.py:1469 (see TD-8). Preserve shell-level SIGTERM handling so the wrapper exits cleanly on orchestrator signal. Covered in Track 6.

findings.title: QUESTION message type has 11+ call sites across production, tests, and docs
findings.description: Grep across the codebase confirms QUESTION is not merely a test-fixture type — it has 4 production call sites (enum definition, BRC_HISTORY_TYPES frozenset at pipelines.py:4775, reviewer-preamble active advertisement at pipelines.py:6062-6074, CLI --type acceptance), 6 test-file references (4 substantive test functions in test_brc_history.py plus assertions in test_concurrent_integration.py:165-174,424,451), and 1 docs reference. The reviewer-preamble advertisement is particularly significant: it tells reviewers to use QUESTION for clarification. Removing the type without removing this preamble section would cause runtime errors when reviewers follow the preamble's advice.
findings.remediation: Track 5 scope enumerates all 11 sites: (a) MessageType enum removal, (b) BRC_HISTORY_TYPES entry removal, (c) reviewer-preamble removal + replacement text ('to request clarification, NACK with the question inline; avoid bus-free question messaging — it is not delivered as an addressed event'), (d) 4 test_brc_history.py test function rewrites, (e) 3 test_concurrent_integration.py assertion updates, (f) docs/guides/concurrent-execution.md removal, (g) CLI-level deprecation error when --type QUESTION is passed, (h) docs/reference/agent-wait-patterns.md migration note. All landed atomically in one commit (no green/red window).

findings.title: mission.md polling guidance is minimal and not surfaced in preamble
findings.description: sandbox/agent-config/rules/mission.md:152 says 'Use egg-orch message poll --wait 30 for long-polling (not sleep loops)' but does not explain WHY, does not name a single idiom, and does not prohibit for-loops. The BRC preamble in pipelines.py does not reference it.
findings.remediation: Create `docs/reference/agent-wait-patterns.md` with a single recommended idiom per scenario, explicit Don'ts, and a 'why' paragraph. Reference from mission.md and from the BRC preamble. Covered in Track 1.

technical_decisions.title: Server-side typed wait is a loop over XREAD BLOCK, not a new Redis structure
technical_decisions.rationale: XREAD BLOCK with Python-side type/role filtering already works and requires no new Redis state.
technical_decisions.implications: get_messages(..., wait=N) returns all matching messages; the new wait_for_typed helper filters inside the server loop and returns on first match. Thin layer; no schema changes.

technical_decisions.title: In-memory blocking uses threading.Condition, not threading.Event
technical_decisions.rationale: Multiple waiters must be notified on any append (role filtering happens after wake). Condition + notify_all is the canonical pattern.
technical_decisions.implications: InMemoryMessageStore gains `_cond = threading.Condition(self._lock)`. append_message calls `self._cond.notify_all()` while holding the lock. clear() also calls notify_all to wake pending waiters at phase transitions (RISK-5). Tests cover two-waiter case and clear-wake case.

technical_decisions.title: HEARTBEAT state is emitted on transitions, not periodically — with HARD rate limit at send_message, not just overseer log
technical_decisions.rationale: Periodic heartbeats recreate the bus-pollution pathology. Transition-based emission bounds count by state-change events (<10 per phase). Hard rate limit prevents a buggy agent from flooding the bus.
technical_decisions.implications: Agents emit HEARTBEAT on: start (WORKING), work done (PROPOSED if producer / IDLE if reviewer), waiting on peer (WAITING_ON_ROLE), consensus (CONFIRMED). No timer-driven emission. Send_message validation at routes/messages.py returns 429 when an agent exceeds EGG_HEARTBEAT_RATE_LIMIT (default 20/min). HealthMonitor._on_message_sent resets last_heartbeat on HEARTBEAT — wiring is a REQUIRED downstream consumer change (RISK-2, blocking-3).

technical_decisions.title: QUESTION removal is a hard delete — atomic across 11 call sites in one commit
technical_decisions.rationale: Atomic removal avoids test green/red windows. Zero deprecation window: Q3 HITL confirms additions are safe and removals of tracked-but-unused symbols are similarly safe for in-flight pipelines.
technical_decisions.implications: Single commit touches 4 production sites, 6 test files, and 1 docs file. Reviewer-preamble replacement text explains the behavioural change: clarifications happen via NACK. CLI-level deprecation error on --type QUESTION. See F7 / RISK-1.

technical_decisions.title: consensus_wrapper uses `message wait --for CONSENSUS_REACHED`, not SSE
technical_decisions.rationale: The wrapper is a shell script wrapper. message wait provides a single-command event-driven block that respects SIGTERM via the existing shell trap.
technical_decisions.implications: Wrapper shell loop becomes at most one outer `while true; do egg-orch message wait --for CONSENSUS_REACHED || break; done` (canonical idiom) or a single invocation if EGG_MESSAGE_POLL_MAX_WAIT covers the expected stay-alive window. SIGTERM trap unchanged. CONSENSUS_REACHED is the new MessageType added in Track 5 (see TD-8). Exit-code contract comes from TD-10.

technical_decisions.title: Env var naming — EGG_MESSAGE_POLL_MAX_WAIT, EGG_HEARTBEAT_RATE_LIMIT
technical_decisions.implications: Defaults preserve behavior (60s cap, 20/min HB rate). Operators who raise EGG_MESSAGE_POLL_MAX_WAIT must raise HTTP proxy idle timeout; startup warn above 60.

technical_decisions.title: Preamble wording: imperative single idiom, not descriptive alternatives
technical_decisions.rationale: LLMs follow explicit imperative instructions better. Per Q5 HITL.
technical_decisions.implications: Final preamble text: 'STAY ALIVE: Run `while true; do egg-orch message wait --for CONSENSUS_REACHED || break; done`. Do NOT wrap this in a for-loop. Do NOT call `sleep N`. Do NOT poll in iterations — the command blocks until a matching message arrives or the timeout elapses.' (Uses the new MessageType.CONSENSUS_REACHED per TD-8.)

technical_decisions.title: New MessageType.CONSENSUS_REACHED emitted alongside CONSENSUS_CONFIRMED for the final flavour ONLY
technical_decisions.rationale: Reviewer_plan NACK blocking-1 established that signals.py:1456-1471 uses the SAME MessageType.CONSENSUS_CONFIRMED for both pending (metadata={'pending_acks': True}) and final (metadata={'consensus_reached': bool}). A type-filtering primitive cannot distinguish them. Picked option (a) from NACK: introduce a new MessageType.CONSENSUS_REACHED emitted at signals.py:1469 IN ADDITION TO (not replacing) the existing CONSENSUS_CONFIRMED final emission. Additive, safe for existing consumers, cheap for the wait primitive to filter.
technical_decisions.implications: Two writes per final consensus instead of one — acceptable (<=3 agents x 1 final confirmation per phase = tiny volume). CONSENSUS_CONFIRMED semantics unchanged for existing consumers (BRC_HISTORY_TYPES, audit logging, metrics). message wait --for CONSENSUS_REACHED only matches the final flavour. Tests must verify pending_acks emissions do NOT emit CONSENSUS_REACHED.

technical_decisions.title: message wait supports --since ID for resumability
technical_decisions.rationale: NACK non-blocking nb-4: after a transport-error retry, the canonical idiom must not double-deliver. --since lets the client resume from the last-seen message ID.
technical_decisions.implications: Server-side wait loop starts XREAD BLOCK from since_id on each retry. Same semantics as message poll's --since. CLI flag: `--since <ID>` optional; when absent, starts from newest messages only (matches current message poll default behaviour for wait>0).

technical_decisions.title: message wait exit codes
technical_decisions.rationale: Wrapper (track-6) needs a deterministic exit-code contract to classify outcomes without parsing stdout.
technical_decisions.implications: Exit codes: 0 = match found (stdout: matching message JSON), 1 = timeout with no match (stdout: empty array '[]'), 2 = transient connection failure (stdout: error message on stderr). Wrapper retries exit 2 with backoff; treats 0 and 1 as the outer-loop continue/exit conditions per TD-5.

constraints: No backwards-incompatible bus schema change for in-flight pipelines — additions (HEARTBEAT, CONSENSUS_REACHED) are safe; removal of QUESTION is safe because agents ignore unknowns and all 11 call sites land atomically.
EGG_MESSAGE_STORE_BACKEND=memory must truly block on wait > 0 — load-bearing for local dev (HITL Q2).
HTTP proxy idle timeout (gateway.egg-system.svc.cluster.local:3129) is the hard cap — raising EGG_MESSAGE_POLL_MAX_WAIT above 60s requires coordinated gateway config change.
consensus_wrapper SIGTERM handling must be preserved so orchestrator graceful-shutdown classification (exit 0 vs 1) still works.
BRC preamble is shared across all concurrent-mode agents — tests in orchestrator/tests/test_pipeline_prompts.py lock in structure.
HealthMonitor._on_message_sent wiring change (Track 5) is a REQUIRED consumer change — without it, agents that migrate to HEARTBEAT messaging trip heartbeat_timeout alerts (RISK-2, blocking-3).
CONSENSUS_REACHED emission is additive — existing CONSENSUS_CONFIRMED emissions remain unchanged so metrics, audit, and downstream consumers keep working.

QUESTION test-fixture removal must happen atomically in the same commit as the enum removal; reviewer-preamble (pipelines.py:6062-6074) must be removed in the same commit to avoid advertising a removed type.
WSGI worker pool sizing (Track 7) must ship BEFORE track 3 goes live in production — otherwise 30-70 long-poll sockets exhaust the default worker count (RISK-3).

complexity_assessment.reasoning: Seven tracks across prompt scaffolding, CLI, HTTP routes, Redis plumbing, in-memory store, message vocabulary, consensus wrapper, HealthMonitor wiring, WSGI deployment config, tests, and docs. Each track is independently mergeable but must land in a specific order to avoid CI green/red windows. Concurrency risk in track-4 (Condition correctness + clear() wake). Cross-module wiring in track-5 (message_store + signals + health_monitor + CLI + preamble + BRC_HISTORY_TYPES). 11 atomic call-site changes for QUESTION removal. Estimate 10-14 commits in a single PR, with tests added alongside each change.
